picks.name: Alphabet Inc.

picks.name: Meta Platforms Inc.

picks.catalyst: Q2 2026 earnings on July 29 — ad revenue growth, AI ROAS data, and any capex guidance revision vs. the $125-145B full-year guide

picks.name: S&P Global Inc.
picks.rationale: SPGI is a high-quality financial data and ratings oligopoly with secular tailwinds from debt issuance (late-cycle credit markets generating ratings revenue), index proliferation, and AI-powered financial intelligence. The consensus from 24 analysts is 'Strong Buy' with a 12-month price target implying ~23.3% upside. BofA remains constructive into Q2 earnings, and Baird raised their target to $521. The macro regime — elevated rates driving debt refinancing activity, rising IPO/M&A volumes boosting Platts and Capital IQ — is directly accretive to all three SPGI revenue segments. This is the 'toll booth on capital markets' trade with a moat that deepens in volatility.
picks.catalyst: Q2 2026 earnings (expected late July/early August) with ratings revenue acceleration and Capital IQ AI product adoption metrics
picks.entryNote: Current price ~$420 vs. 12-month consensus target ~$518; trading below its 5-year median multiple on a P/E basis despite superior earnings quality; BofA lowered PT to $550 from $575 but maintained Buy — the reset creates a more attractive entry
picks.exitTrigger: Debt issuance volumes collapse (credit market freeze) OR antitrust action against rating agency duopoly pricing; revenue growth below 8% for two consecutive quarters
picks.keyRisk: A credit market seizure (HY spreads blowing past 600 bps) would crater new issuance ratings revenue and simultaneously impair the data services segment via client budget cuts

picks.name: RTX Corporation
picks.rationale: RTX is a dual-engine defense-aerospace compounder benefiting from the highest defense capex cycle since the Cold War (NATO rearmament, Middle East conflict driving munitions demand) AND a commercial aerospace aftermarket recovery as global air traffic normalizes. The macro context explicitly calls out defense contractors (LMT, RTX, NOC) as 'regime's clearest fundamental beneficiaries' with Brent crude above $95/bbl sustaining geopolitical risk premiums. The sector rotation data shows Industrials as Tier 1 overweight, and RTX specifically benefits from the 'One Big Beautiful Bill' defense spending allocation. Backlog visibility extends 4–6 years, providing earnings certainty rare in this macro regime.
picks.catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings with Pratt & Whitney GTF engine shop visit revenue ramp and any new DoD/NATO contract wins announced amid ongoing Middle East tensions
picks.catalystWindow: October 2026 earnings + any defense contract award announcements in next 60 days
picks.entryNote: Trading at approximately 22–24x forward earnings — in line with 5-year average for a quality defense compounder; YTD performance has been strong but the forward backlog (multi-year) is not fully priced; a re-escalation of Iran conflict is a direct positive catalyst
picks.exitTrigger: Pratt & Whitney GTF engine grounding escalation imposing material liability OR a credible ceasefire agreement that structurally reduces NATO defense spending commitments
picks.keyRisk: GTF engine inspection/repair program cost overruns creating unexpected cash outflows and margin compression beyond the already-disclosed remediation budget

picks.name: Micron Technology Inc.
picks.rationale: Micron is the primary beneficiary of the HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) supercycle driven by AI accelerator demand, with HBM revenue ramping to represent the largest incremental margin driver in the company's history. The momentum screen scores MU at 19/25 with 4/4 EPS beats and massive FY estimate upward revisions. Druckenmiller rotated from GOOGL into memory plays including MU and SNDK, explicitly betting on the AI infrastructure components layer over the hyperscalers themselves — a high-quality smart money signal. Today's oil price pullback (Brent to $95) reduces inflationary pressure on DRAM production costs.
picks.catalyst: Q4 FY2026 earnings in late September with HBM revenue disclosure and FY2027 HBM supply allocation commentary
picks.entryNote: MU sits in a position of mean-reversion risk given extraordinary TTM gains, but HBM structural demand (AI accelerator content per chip increasing) justifies a higher normalized valuation floor; use any pullback toward prior consolidation as an incremental add
picks.exitTrigger: HBM order deferral or cancellation from NVDA or hyperscalers; DRAM spot price reversal signaling inventory overbuild; export control tightening on HBM to China
picks.keyRisk: Memory is inherently cyclical — if AI training workloads plateau or training efficiency improves dramatically (DeepSeek-style), HBM demand growth could stall before Micron's capacity investments are fully monetized

picks.name: Quanta Services Inc.
picks.rationale: Quanta is the dominant electrical infrastructure and grid modernization contractor in the U.S., directly benefiting from the AI data center power demand surge (U.S. power demand potentially setting a 2026 record), the Inflation Reduction Act electrification buildout, and the 'One Big Beautiful Bill' grid spending. The sector rotation scorecard explicitly highlights increased capital spending in electricity capacity and AI infrastructure as the core Industrials thesis, and Quanta has no-bid competitive positions on large utility transmission contracts with multi-year visibility. The macro context — with VST and CEG as power generators — makes PWR the 'picks and shovels' play on the same theme.
picks.catalyst: Q2 2026 earnings report with backlog update and any new grid/transmission contract awards tied to hyperscaler data center power agreements
picks.entryNote: PWR has performed in line with SPY YTD but the backlog and contract pipeline have grown faster than price — multiple is reasonable vs. the growth visibility it offers; a confirmed Brent pullback today reduces near-term cost inflation fears for construction materials
picks.exitTrigger: Backlog growth stalls below 10% YoY OR utility capex programs face regulatory delay that pushes major transmission projects out of the 5-year plan
picks.keyRisk: Labor cost inflation in skilled electrical trades squeezes project margins; supply chain delays in transformer and high-voltage equipment extend project timelines and defer revenue recognition

picks.name: Vistra Energy Corp.
picks.rationale: Vistra is the largest competitive power generator in the U.S. and a pure-play beneficiary of the AI data center power demand supercycle, with merchant power pricing power in ERCOT (Texas) where data center load growth is most concentrated. Tepper's Appaloosa doubled its VST position in Q1 2026, making it a key smart money conviction name in the power/AI intersection. The sector rotation data explicitly names VST as an AI data center power demand beneficiary, and with U.S. power demand potentially setting a 2026 record, Vistra's contracted and merchant generation assets are structurally re-pricing upward. Today's oil pullback reduces natural gas substitute costs, improving Vistra's competitive position.
picks.catalyst: Q2 2026 earnings with ERCOT merchant power pricing disclosures and any new data center offtake agreement announcements
picks.entryNote: VST is classified as Utilities but trades as a growth stock given its merchant exposure; the AI power narrative gives it a hybrid growth/defensive characteristic; Tepper's doubling of the position in Q1 provides institutional backing with a sophisticated macro overlay
picks.exitTrigger: ERCOT regulatory repricing that caps merchant power rates OR a major data center tenant postpones load commitments, reducing contracted revenue visibility for 2027+
picks.keyRisk: Extreme weather events in Texas (ERCOT is islanded) creating forced outage liability; alternatively, AI power demand growth disappoints relative to the contracted capacity Vistra is building

picks.name: CrowdStrike Holdings Inc.
picks.rationale: CrowdStrike delivered strong Q1 FY2027 results with record net new ARR, increased annual revenue guidance, and Wells Fargo raised the price target to $900 — and the 4-for-1 stock split effective July 2 has improved retail accessibility and broadened the shareholder base. picks.catalyst: Q2 FY2027 earnings in September 2026 with net new ARR and AI security module (Charlotte AI) adoption metrics; any major state-sponsored cyberattack attribution event accelerates enterprise contract urgency
picks.catalystWindow: September 2026 earnings + ongoing geopolitical threat environment
picks.entryNote: Post-split price structure; RSI moved through oversold (21 on July 14) before the July 14 cyber rally — the technical setup suggests the worst of the post-split digestion is past; valuation at ~137x forward earnings remains demanding but justified by 95%+ gross retention and expanding platform revenue per customer
picks.exitTrigger: Net Revenue Retention rate falls below 115% for two consecutive quarters OR a second major product-related outage (similar to July 2024) that triggers mass customer churn
picks.keyRisk: Valuation at 137x forward earnings leaves no room for any execution miss; a broader software multiple compression driven by rising Treasury yields (10-year toward 5%) could de-rate the stock significantly even without any fundamental deterioration

picks.name: SPDR Gold Shares ETF
picks.rationale: Gold is the premier hard currency hedge in a fiscal dominance / stagflation-risk regime — the 30-year Treasury at 5.17% (longest stretch above 5% since 2007), CPI at 3.5% YoY, and the FOMC raising its 2026 inflation outlook to 3.6% all support gold as a real asset alternative to duration. Spot gold pulled back from an all-time high of $5,300/oz to ~$4,100/oz (GLD ~$379 as of July 22), creating a meaningful re-entry opportunity. Central bank demand remains structurally elevated and today's oil pullback on Iran ceasefire hopes (Brent to $95) provides a transient headwind that reinforces the buy-on-dips thesis rather than invalidating it.
picks.catalyst: Hot July 30 PCE print re-accelerating core inflation validates stagflation narrative; any FOMC rate hike in September converts bond investors into gold holders
picks.entryNote: GLD ~$379, pulling back ~28% from ATH of ~$488 equivalent — a significant discount to recent peak; 200-day moving average provides technical support; China central bank accumulation provides structural demand floor
picks.exitTrigger: Core PCE decelerates convincingly to 2.2% or below for three consecutive months, signaling the Fed can credibly ease — reducing gold's real-rate appeal
picks.keyRisk: A credible U.S.-Iran ceasefire combined with a surprise dovish FOMC pivot (September cut instead of hike) would create a dual headwind — lower geopolitical premium and stronger real rates alternative

picks.name: Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF
picks.rationale: SCHD provides diversified exposure to high-quality dividend compounders with a proven screen for financial health, dividend growth consistency, and reasonable valuations — precisely the factor profile that outperforms in late-cycle/stagflation regimes when growth stocks face multiple compression. With the 30-year Treasury at 5.17%, SCHD's dividend yield (~3.5–4%) must compete with fixed income but compensates with earnings growth and dividend escalation that bonds cannot replicate. SCHD's holdings screen for low debt/equity and consistent FCF — the opposite risk profile from the AI capex-heavy mega-caps dominating the growth book.
picks.catalyst: Any Fed rate cut signal in 2027 re-rates dividend equity vs. fixed income; Q3 dividend declaration season in October confirms yield sustainability
picks.catalystWindow: Ongoing income accrual; re-rating catalyst in 2027 if Fed pivots
picks.entryNote: SCHD is modestly below its 52-week high after underperforming growth in Q1-Q2 2026; yield is competitive with short-dated IG credit at current prices; entry at current levels locks in an attractive starting yield with dividend growth optionality
picks.exitTrigger: Sustained dividend cuts across SCHD top holdings (>15% of portfolio cutting dividends) indicating a broad earnings recession; or SCHD yield premium over 2-year Treasury narrows below 50 bps
picks.keyRisk: A hard landing that forces dividend cuts across industrials and financials (the two largest SCHD sector weights) compresses both price and yield simultaneously

picks.name: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. Class B
picks.rationale: Berkshire under Greg Abel is the single best 'fortress in a risk-off event' in the equity universe — a $397B cash hoard (the largest in history), diversified across insurance, energy, rails, and consumer staples, with low AI capex exposure and the optionality to deploy capital aggressively in a market dislocation. Abel restarted buybacks ($235M in Q1), made the portfolio leaner (from 40 to 26 positions), and tripled the GOOGL stake — demonstrating conviction without recklessness. In a late-cycle regime where HY OAS at 269 bps signals complacency, BRK.B is the one large-cap that becomes a buyer when everyone else is a forced seller.
picks.catalyst: Any major market dislocation (credit event, AI capex reset) triggers BRK.B's acquisition playbook — Abel deploying the $397B cash hoard is a stock-specific re-rating catalyst independent of the broader market
picks.catalystWindow: Ongoing; any market drawdown of 15%+ in next 12 months
picks.entryNote: Trading at approximately 1.4–1.5x book — not cheap historically but justified by the float-funded insurance operation and the unprecedented cash optionality; low beta (~0.7x) provides natural portfolio dampening
picks.exitTrigger: Abel makes a major acquisition at a clearly inflated price that destroys capital discipline — the Buffett legacy's primary protection against this risk is now reliant on Abel's judgment
picks.keyRisk: GEICO underwriting deterioration from climate-related claims or auto insurance adverse development; alternatively, a prolonged period of low-volatility markets means the $397B cash drag becomes an opportunity cost headwind

picks.name: iShares 7-10 Year Treasury ETF
picks.rationale: IEF serves as the portfolio's flight-to-safety put — in a genuine risk-off scenario triggered by an AI capex disappointment, credit market seizure, or geopolitical shock, intermediate-duration Treasuries rally sharply as capital flees risk assets. With the 10-year at 4.68% and the 30-year at 5.17%, IEF offers the highest starting yield since the 2007–2008 era while providing zero credit risk. The July 30 PCE + Q2 GDP data creates a binary event — a soft PCE print would generate an immediate IEF rally; a hot print would add a modest headwind but the yield cushion absorbs some of it.
picks.catalyst: July 30 PCE print softer than the FOMC's 3.3% core estimate; any Fed pivot signal or AI capex reset triggering risk-off flows into Treasuries
picks.entryNote: IEF at current prices offers ~4.2% running yield — the highest entry yield in 15+ years; the 10-year at 4.68% is near the upper range of the post-2022 rate regime; position sizing is deliberately modest (5%) as a hedge, not a conviction long
picks.exitTrigger: 10-year Treasury yield spikes above 5.25% with no recession signal (fiscal dominance scenario) making longer duration untenable; or Fed credibly signals rate hikes above 4.5%, rendering intermediate Treasuries mark-to-market negative
picks.keyRisk: Fiscal dominance — the 'One Big Beautiful Bill' deficit trajectory ($3-4T over 10 years) could push long-end yields structurally higher, creating sustained mark-to-market losses that offset the yield income

picks.name: The Coca-Cola Company
picks.rationale: Coca-Cola is the ultimate late-cycle consumer staples compounder — pricing power globally, dividend aristocrat (62 consecutive years of dividend increases), and Berkshire's third-largest holding at 11.56% of the portfolio (Buffett has held since 1988, Abel has maintained). In a stagflation regime with real purchasing power under pressure, KO's inelastic demand and international revenue diversification (~60% non-US) provides genuine earnings stability. With CPI at 3.5% YoY, KO's ability to implement annual price increases across its beverage portfolio protects real earnings in ways that most consumer discretionary names cannot match.
picks.catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings with organic revenue growth and pricing update; any Fed rate cut signal in 2027 re-rates dividend stalwarts vs. money market alternatives
picks.catalystWindow: Q3 earnings October 2026 + 2027 rate cycle turn
picks.entryNote: KO trading at approximately 22–23x forward earnings — modest premium to staples peer group but justified by the brand moat and global distribution; forward yield ~3.0% is competitive with short-dated IG credit at current prices after tax; Berkshire's conviction hold provides a valuation floor
picks.exitTrigger: Organic volume growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters globally, OR GLP-1 adoption materially reduces beverage consumption patterns in the U.S. consumer data
picks.keyRisk: Sugar/commodity cost inflation re-accelerates (Iran conflict / energy shock impacting agricultural transport costs), compressing gross margins before the next round of price increases can be implemented

summary: The portfolio operates in a confirmed late-cycle / stagflation-risk regime: GDP growth intact (+3.0% GDPNow Q2), but the 30-year Treasury at 5.17%, CPI at 3.5% YoY, and a hawkish FOMC (>80% probability of September hike) create a high-friction environment for multiple expansion. The 10-name growth book expresses this via a barbell of AI-infrastructure compounders with earnings-per-share momentum (AVGO, GOOGL post-massive Q2 beat, META into July 29 earnings, MU on HBM ramp) against macro-regime beneficiaries with real asset backing (GS on yield curve re-steepening and capital markets cycle, RTX on defense spending acceleration, PWR/VST on the AI power demand supercycle, CRWD on geopolitically-accelerated cyber spending) and a financial data oligopoly with 23% upside per consensus (SPGI). All ten growth names are carry-overs from the prior week's positioning with thesis continuity confirmed — GOOGL's massive Q2 EPS beat ($9.11 vs $2.87 est.) reinforces the conviction hold despite post-earnings capex selloff, and today's Brent pullback to $95/bbl (Iran ceasefire hopes) provides a transient relief to the inflation backdrop without invalidating the structural energy/defense thesis. The five-name defensive sleeve (GLD as stagflation/real-asset hedge, SCHD for dividend-growth ballast, BRK.B as the fortress with $397B cash optionality, IEF as the risk-off put at a 15-year high starting yield, KO as the pricing-power consumer staples anchor held by Berkshire) collectively provide downside protection across the dominant tail risks: AI capex deflation, fiscal dominance rate spike, and Middle East escalation. The dominant risk being underwritten is an AI capex reset that simultaneously de-rates the three AI-infrastructure names (AVGO, MU, CRWD) in the growth book — managed by the SPGI/GS/RTX/PWR/VST diversification into non-AI-correlated earnings streams.
diversificationNote: The 10-name growth book spans 5 GICS sectors: Information Technology (AVGO, MU, CRWD), Communication Services (GOOGL, META), Financials (GS, SPGI), Industrials (RTX, PWR), and Utilities (VST) — the 3-name IT maximum constraint is satisfied; the two Communication Services names (GOOGL search/cloud vs. META social/ad-tech) operate in different end markets despite sharing the sector label. The defensive sleeve spans 5 distinct exposures: gold (GLD), broad dividend equity (SCHD), diversified insurance/financial compounder (BRK.B), intermediate-duration Treasuries (IEF), and consumer staples brand equity (KO) — no exposure is doubled. Accepted factor concentration: three growth names (AVGO, MU, CRWD) share AI infrastructure secular exposure but operate at different points in the stack (custom silicon, memory, cybersecurity) with different customer bases and cycle timing.
